clue.text: New EU ban's enraged beef producer

indicators.note: a new version of the words that follow puts their letters in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
the S of the possessive counts as a letter here
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a new European ban on a breed of cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enraged' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'New' makes the anagram of EU BAN'S ENRAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish black hornless breed of cattle is raised chiefly for its meat.

clue.text: Flight arrives with planes flying diamonds in

indicators.note: signals that the shuffled letters go inside the arriving word

parts.note: to appear is to arrive

indicators.note: letters flying about land in a new order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for the suit of diamonds in cards

explanation.surface: Air traffic: aircraft fly in carrying diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: the phrase rhymes with stairs, a flight of steps. 'flying' scrambles PLANES with D into PLESANDP.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang this phrase stands for stairs, a flight of steps.

clue.text: Drama queen's raised petition outside

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed around the queen's letter
in a down entry raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to sue is to petition
QU is a standard abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A theatrical queen lifts a petition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drama queen' is a false phrase: 'Drama' is the definition, Peter Shaffer's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Equus is Peter Shaffer's 1973 stage play about a boy who blinds horses.

clue.text: Far from well, daughter digested everything

parts.note: to digest a text is to read it
fully means in every respect, entirely

explanation.surface: A sick daughter who has eaten everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digested' suggests eating; it is reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadfully means very badly, the opposite of well.

clue.text: Sculptor's genius, quietly replacing hip

indicators.note: one piece takes the place of another inside the word for genius

parts.note: Einstein is the archetypal genius
in means fashionable, hip
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A sculptor's brilliance, used softly in place of a hip.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob Epstein was a 20th-century sculptor; 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was a famous modernist sculptor.

clue.text: Really getting into trouble on cycle

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
a ring is a cycle, as in Wagner's

explanation.surface: Somebody gets into difficulties while out on a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the pieces; 'cycle' suggests a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: To be really into someone is to dote on them.

clue.text: Ultimately opting for samosa, plain nan

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the next four words is taken

explanation.surface: Choosing a samosa over plain naan bread in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nan' looks like the Indian bread; it is a granny.
explanation.definitionFit: Nan is a familiar British name for a grandmother.

clue.text: Design fiction, keeping credibility W initially within sight

parts.note: spec, a specification, is a design

indicators.note: the story holds the next letter within it

parts.note: a tale is fiction

indicators.note: only the first letter of credibility is used

explanation.surface: A design story keeps credibility within view.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray W is an OCR mark; 'within' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a remarkable sight.

clue.text: Girl in Omsk let love develop for Moscow student

indicators.note: letters that develop take on a new form

parts.note: love is zero, O, in tennis

explanation.surface: A girl in a Siberian city allows romance to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kremlinologist studies the Soviet government, which sat in Moscow's Kremlin.

clue.text: First trace of pigment, unrefined, used in blusher?

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word pigment is all that is taken

parts.note: unrefined manners are rude ones

explanation.surface: Advice on putting a little crude colour into a cosmetic for the cheeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blusher' looks like make-up, but here it is a person who blushes easily, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A prim, easily shocked person blushes at anything improper, so is jokingly a blusher.

clue.text: Use catchphrases from big hit — a sound approach

parts.note: to slog the ball is to hit it hard

indicators.note: the word before it, approach, is taken by how it is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to approach is to near

explanation.surface: Advice to coin catchy phrases, with a sporting image of a big hit as a sensible method.
explanation.definitionFit: To sloganeer is to coin or repeat slogans, the catchphrases of campaigns and advertising.

clue.text: Midshipman studies computing in order to relax

parts.note: Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of a novel by Captain Marryat
to do a subject is to study it
IT, information technology, is computing

explanation.surface: A young naval officer takes a computing course to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Midshipman Easy is an 1836 sea novel by Frederick Marryat, a once-famous British book.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a spoken plea to take things gently and calmly, much like saying relax.

clue.text: Bit of make-up seen on cover of address book one of two?

annotationWithheld.why: Bit of make-up seen on cover of address book one of two? (4): A (cover of address) and TOM can be found, but no reading accounts for both 'book' and 'one of two' without a word doing two jobs or nothing
annotationWithheld.clue: Bit of make-up seen on cover of address book one of two?

clue.text: Double round: fix an eggnog whatsit

indicators.note: double means the letter that follows is written twice

parts.note: O is round in shape
a jam is a fix or predicament
an is the article a
a flip is a drink of beaten egg and spirit

explanation.surface: Two rounds of drinks: fixing an eggnog thing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a jokey name for a thing whose name escapes one, like a thingummy.

clue.text: Break old vase found on a record player

parts.note: a disc jockey plays records
an urn is a large vase

explanation.surface: An antique vase sits atop a gramophone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record player' suggests a gramophone, but it is a person: the DJ.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjourn a meeting is to break off proceedings for a time.

clue.text: Flight spelling bird's premature end

definitions.meaning: bird is time in jail, ended early by breaking out

explanation.surface: An escape that spells an early end for a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is slang for a prison term (birdlime, time); 'spelling' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakout from prison is a flight that cuts short a sentence.

clue.text: Hollow green organic chestnut with one's dumplings

indicators.note: emptying out a word leaves only its outer letters, here for both green and organic

parts.note: ch is the abbreviation for chestnut used of horses' colours
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A recipe of organic chestnut and greens made into dumplings.
explanation.walkthrough: CH for chestnut comes from racing form, where a horse's colour is abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small Italian dumplings, usually of potato or semolina.

clue.text: Winger repelled by obstruction a tiny bit

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the winger word is read backwards

parts.note: a bird is a creature with wings
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A football winger is pushed back by a defender's tiny obstruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' looks like a footballer; it is a bird. 'repelled' reverses BIRD to DRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A driblet is a small drop or a trifling amount.

clue.text: Pretty short period of time for speaker

parts.note: twee means quaintly pretty

indicators.note: cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: A rather brief spell of time before a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is a small loudspeaker for high frequencies.

clue.text: Lab cope somehow, producing medicine

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A laboratory muddles through and turns out a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy medicine given for its psychological effect.

clue.text: Was jumping cat seen in Palladium?

indicators.note: the cat is shown inside the symbol

parts.note: Pd is the chemical symbol for palladium
an ounce is a snow leopard

explanation.surface: A cat spotted at the London Palladium theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The London Palladium is a famous West End theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To pounce is to leap suddenly.

clue.text: Island resort: you must turn up to it

indicators.note: an instruction to turn the phrase that follows, so its synonym is read backwards

parts.note: someone up to it is able

explanation.surface: A holiday island where visitors are told they have to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reads as arrive; split it, 'turn' is the reversal and 'up to it' is ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is a Mediterranean island off Tuscany, now a holiday destination.

clue.text: Elaborate dress with split for zip

parts.note: a getup is an elaborate outfit
and means together with
to split is to leave, go

explanation.surface: A fancy dress with a slit fastened by a zip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zip' looks like a fastener for the dress; it is energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip means energy and drive, which is what this phrase describes.

clue.text: Flatter club that has no sign of victory

indicators.note: the club word loses a letter

parts.note: a driver is a golf club
the V sign signals victory

explanation.surface: A club that has not won is flattering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like a verb; it is an adjective, more dry and dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Drier wine or humour is flatter, less lively.

clue.text: Old woman breaking leg in a state

indicators.note: the woman word splits the cricket word open

parts.note: leg side is on side in cricket
old woman is slang for mother, ma; that the answer also sits inside the clue word woman is a coincidence

explanation.surface: An elderly lady breaking a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Creaking sounds from space next to loft

indicators.note: the letters entered are heard in the words that follow rather than spelt

parts.note: space is a room and a loft is an attic, so room next to attic is what is said

explanation.surface: Noises coming from a room by the attic, as in an old house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next to' joins ROOM and ATTIC; said aloud they give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatic joints are stiff and painful, so a rheumatic person creaks.

clue.text: Italian's regularly giving out alluring air

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the words alluring and air at a steady interval

explanation.surface: An Italian man's attractive manner is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A typical Italian man's name, standing for an Italian.

clue.text: Close friend generous with cherry brandy?

parts.note: kind means generous
cherry is a shade of red
brandy is a spirit

explanation.surface: A good friend who is generous with a drink of cherry brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A soulmate whose outlook matches one's own is a close friend.
